summary:
Lane B of HTML v2.74 is finished, and so is the v2.74 deliverable set for both lanes. The final file is /home/user/Cartalith_GDT/html/Cartalith v2.74 DCC test.html, md5 bc0559a4ec776578672ba31c88d46ecd.

What lane B built:
- V26, the corners (Ruling EC item 7). v2.23's `*{border-radius:0 !important}` is removed. Five tokens now hold every radius, pointer value then touch value: --r-btn 16/12, --r-tile 14/12, --r-field 12, --r-menu 10, --r-pill 999px. Pointer values are the newer design canvas's. Touch takes the port's touch radius, 12 (DccTheme btn_radius [8,12]), because hit-testing follows border-radius and the design's 24px touch pills broke v2.73's corner-press guarantee. DS-13's round buttons keep their whole box as the target through an empty ::after.
- Surfaces stay square: panels, docks, bands, windows, menus, popovers, cards and the map. Rows, tabs and the rail are squared by one rule.
- `.seg` is one rounded container that clips its square children. New World's grid no longer doubles its edge divider, and the D-block "flat" comment is corrected.
- All 101 radius declarations the reset had silenced are decided where they are written: 66 in the stylesheet, 35 inline. 26 kept, 10 moved to a token, 65 removed.
- V24 (owner default Q5): an armed segment is a washed chip drawn 2px inside it. The fill stays only on tool-mode segments: `[data-civtool]` palettes and Sculpt's feature picker. Armed pills and the Base map row are washed too.
- Dock segments are mono 10/500/.08em, sized to their labels with no wrapping inside a segment. Dock action buttons are mono uppercase, CIVIL's five sub-tabs are mono 500, and Bake and Un-finalize run full width.
- V25: one section-label rule over the nine selectors; location labels keep the accent.
- V29: the strip's filters are washed chips around visually hidden, focusable checkboxes. The year pill's ✕ moved to --dim.
- V30: one window-heading rule, mono 11px 500 .2em uppercase accent; the City viewer is exempt.
- Two extra contrast fixes: the Types tab's quarters line, and the year-pill ✕.

Deliverables for both lanes: #verTag and VERSION read v2.74; tests/perf/probe_fixpass.js (RC style, usage header matches the code); tests/perf/shots_v274.js; 16 screenshots in evidence/v2.74/, all 16 opened and looked at; CHANGELOG_v2.74.md and CLAUDE_v2.74.md in RC format; the README's table, stage plan and verify commands. No placeholders are left.

The changelog states the toll fix's changed planner results (lane A's text) and every owner default taken, by question Q1 to Q14. It also lists every departure from the design and everything that needs a person on a device.

judgement_calls: Touch radius is 12, the port's DccTheme btn_radius touch value and within Ruling EC's 'about 10–16px', not the design's 24px touch pills. Hit-testing follows border-radius, and v2.73's guarantee that a press 4px in from a 44px control's corner still lands failed at 22 and holds at 12. DS-13's round buttons keep the design's round shape with a full-box ::after target.

Pointer radii follow the newer design canvas (buttons 16, tiles 14, fields 12, menu buttons 10, pills 999) over the port's pointer value of 8, which came from the older 2026-09-07 canvas. This applies the rule that the newer canvas wins.

The washed on-state is a chip drawn 2px inside the segment (::before under the label), not a ring on the segment's own box, which the rounded container would cut at the end segments. Segment widths and dividers do not move.

'Tool-mode segment' (Q5's fill exception) means the [data-civtool] Tools palettes plus Sculpt's feature picker. Every other segmented control, armed pill and the Base map popover's picked row is washed.

Every surface is square, including windows' outer frames, menus, popovers, cards, wells and toasts (Ruling EC item 7: 'Panels and bands stay square'). Rows, tabs and the rail are squared by one rule, because a rounded full-width row curves its own divider.
The window heading is 11px, as the design draws it, over the audit plan's 12px. The City viewer's place-name heading is exempt.
CIVIL sub-tabs keep .02em tracking rather than the design's .18em, because at .18em the five need 380px of the 371 the dock has at 1366.
Dock segments take their own label's width, with no wrapping inside a segment. At equal shares the mono labels broke inside the CIVIL tools palette at 1366.

The truncation comparison leaves out the Settlements table (#stTableHead and #stSpacer), because lane A's V01 per-cell ellipsis is intended. Census keys are lower-cased because text-transform changes innerText.
The Types tab's quarters line no longer fades --faint (3.19:1); it uses the hint's ink (4.79). The year pill's ✕ uses --dim, or the pill's ink when armed.

MISTAKES.md candidates (each confirmed in this lane):
1. Rounding a touch target, ×1. Hit-testing follows border-radius: a 44px control with 22px corners no longer contains a point 4px in from its corner, so elementFromPoint returns what is underneath. Root cause: treating the radius as paint only. Rule: on touch, keep corners at 12px or less on 44px targets, or give a round control a full-box `::after` target; re-run probe_mobileshell's corner presses after any radius change. Verify: elementFromPoint at (left+4, top+4) for each touch control. (v2.74 lane B: touch radius 24 failed 4 corner presses on the tablet chevron and DS-13's −.)
2. A universal `!important` reset. v2.23's `*{border-radius:0 !important}` silenced 101 radius declarations for 50 versions, 35 of them inline in the markup and JS templates: a stylesheet `!important` rule beats a non-important inline style. Removing it revives them all at once. Rule: never add a universal `!important` reset. To remove one, inventory the stylesheet and every inline style in the markup and template strings, and decide each.
3. Keying a before/after text census on innerText. innerText returns text after text-transform, so making labels uppercase made the truncation compare report relabelled controls as new. Rule: key text comparisons on lower-cased text (or textContent), and exclude by name any element whose change is intended.
4. Detecting a role versus pinning a value. The 'no armed control draws the accent fill' check compared against the dark theme's accent literal, so on v2.73's light theme, whose accent differs, it passed where it should have failed. Rule: pin literals when asserting what a colour is (the existing rule); when detecting whether a token's role is in use, read the page's own computed token in the forced theme.
